videos.title: The First Person Ever to Receive Bitcoin #shorts
videos.description:
Hal Finney was one of the first people to run the Bitcoin software – in January 2009 he posted "Running bitcoin". On January 12, 2009, Satoshi Nakamoto sent him 10 BTC in block 170: the first bitcoin transaction ever. Later that year Hal was diagnosed with ALS, and he kept programming until he passed away in 2014.

videos.title: Why Does My 3D Printer Poop Plastic? 💩 #shorts
videos.description:
When a multicolor 3D printer switches filament, the old color is still in the nozzle – so it purges plastic until the new color comes out clean. That's roughly 0.3 to 1.5 g per color change, and a model with a few hundred changes can waste 40–90 g, sometimes more than the model itself. Tips: fewer colors per layer, flush into the infill, or print colored parts separately.

Source: https://evezone.

videos.title: Invisible Braces Start in a 3D Printer 🦷 #shorts
videos.description:
Clear aligners like Invisalign start with a scan of your teeth. Each stage of the treatment is 3D printed as a model of your teeth, then clear plastic is heated and formed over it – so every single aligner is unique. Back in 2018, Align Technology made over 320,000 custom aligners per day, and more than 20 million people have been treated.

videos.title: This 3D Print Is Thinner Than a Human Hair 🔬 #shorts
videos.description:
In 2020, physicists at Leiden University 3D printed a 3DBenchy just 30 micrometers long – thinner than a human hair. They used a laser 3D printer (two-photon printing), where the liquid only hardens at the laser's tiny focus point, and used printed shapes like this to study how microswimmers move.

videos.title: This Filament Destroys Your 3D Printer Nozzle ⚠️ #shorts
videos.description:
Glow-in-the-dark filament is packed with strontium aluminate particles – that's what makes it glow, but it's also abrasive. Print after print it grinds away a normal brass nozzle: the hole gets wider and you get under-extrusion and messy prints. The fix: a hardened steel nozzle for glow, carbon fiber and other abrasive filaments.

Source: https://qidi3d.com/blogs/print-lab/glow-in-dark-filament-ti
